# Adjudication Task — Chapter 173

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃173화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|“그럼……?”
  6|
  7|청풍의 놀라움이 섞인 눈빛에 화왕(火王) 적천강은 희미하게 웃어 보였다.
  8|
  9|“나에 대해 들은 바가 있느냐?”
 10|
 11|“할아버지께서 가끔 말씀해 주셨어요.”
 12|
 13|“오호. 그 친구도 나를 잊지 않았나 보구나. 뭐라 하더냐?”
 14|
 15|“무공은 강한데 성격이 좀, 많이 더럽다고 하셨는데요.”
 16|
 17|“…….”
 18|
 19|사실 적천강은 사교성이 그리 좋은 편은 아니었다. 아니, 좋지 않은 정도가 아니라 사실 끔찍한 수준이다.
 20|
 21|어린 시절 온갖 험한 꼴을 겪은 터라 사람에 대한 불신이 뿌리에 박혀 있었고, 그 후에는 괴팍한 성격의 사부 밑에서 자랐다. 그러니 어쩌면 당연한 일일지도 몰랐다.
 22|
 23|“정마대전 때도 하루가 멀다 하고 시비가 붙으셨다고 하던데. 당시 구파일방의 후기지수들은 한 대씩 다 때려 보셨을 거라고…….”
 24|
 25|“크흠, 다 때리긴 누가! 그리고 그때는 젊었으니 그런 것이다. 원래 혈기왕성할 때는…….”
 26|
 27|“당시 환갑이셨던 걸로 아는데요.”
 28|
 29|“커흐흐흠!”
 30|
 31|본전도 못 건진 적천강이 헛기침만 하고 있을 때, 청풍이 한마디를 덧붙였다.
 32|
 33|“그래도 알고 보면 선한 분이니 혹 뵙게 되거든 당신을 대하듯이 하라고 하셨어요.”
 34|
 35|적천강의 입꼬리가 실룩거렸다.
 36|
 37|“음, 매종학 그 친구가 역시 나를 잘 알아.”
 38|
 39|적천강이 정마대전에서 활약한 기간은 일 년 남짓.
 40|
 41|초절정 고수인 두 사람이 같은 전장에 참여하는 일은 드물었고, 매종학과는 열 번 정도 만났을 뿐이지만 지기(知己)라 부를 수 있는 관계인 것은 확실했다.
 42|
 43|‘손자 교육도 아주 잘 시켜 놨군.’
 44|
 45|한데 잠깐, 그가 혼인을 했던가?
 46|
 47|적천강은 청풍의 얼굴을 가만히 뜯어봤다.
 48|
 49|기억 속에 남아 있는 매종학의 얼굴과는 닮은 구석이 하나도 없다.
 50|
 51|‘친손자는 아닌 것 같은데…….’
 52|
 53|뭐, 상관없는 일이다.
 54|
 55|핏줄이 섞였건 안 섞였건 녀석이 그의 후인인 것은 확실해 보였으니까.
 56|
 57|특히 하는 행동이나 말본새를 보면 피가 아니라 영혼이 섞였다고 해도 과언이 아니다.
 58|
 59|적천강은 흐뭇한 웃음을 지으며 청풍에게 말했다.
 60|
 61|“내 오늘 아주 든든한 손주 하나가 생겼구나. 자, 그럼 이 할아비에게 큰절 한 번 올려 보거라.”
 62|
 63|“네?”
 64|
 65|고개를 갸우뚱거린 청풍이 되물었다.
 66|
 67|“왜요?”
 68|
 69|“……왜요라니?”
 70|
 71|순간 당황한 적천강이 말을 더듬었다.
 72|
 73|“매종학이 그 친구가 자신을 대하듯 나를 대하라고 하지 않았더냐?”
 74|
 75|“네.”
 76|
 77|“인석아, 그럼 손주가 할아비를 봤으면 큰절을 올려야지.”
 78|
 79|“저희 할아버지는 그런 거 신경 안 쓰세요. 앞뒤 꽉 막힌 노인네들이나 허례허식에 집착한다고 하셨어요.”
 80|
 81|“……!”
 82|
 83|졸지에 앞뒤 꽉 막힌 노인네가 된 적천강이 몸을 부르르 떨었다.
 84|
 85|“이런 걸 뭐라고 하더라. 얼마 전에 배웠는데.”
 86|
 87|골똘히 생각에 잠겨있던 청풍이 이마를 탁 쳤다.
 88|
 89|“아, 맞다. 꼰대!”
 90|
 91|“꼰, 뭐?”
 92|
 93|“꼰대요. 비슷한 말로 꼰머가 있대요.”
 94|
 95|뭐? 꼰대? 꼰머? 듣기에도 별로고, 어감도 별로다.
 96|
 97|정확히 무슨 말인지는 모르겠으나 맥락은 알 것 같았다.
 98|
 99|‘내가 너무 산에만 틀어박혀 있었나.’
100|
101|장강의 뒷물결은 상상 이상으로 강했다. 그렇다고 하나뿐인 지기의 손주 놈을 두들겨 팰 수도 없고…….
102|
103|적천강은 머리가 띵해지는 걸 느끼며 입을 열었다.
104|
105|“그게 요즘 젊은 놈들 사이에서 유행하는, 뭐 그런 거냐?”
106|
107|“몰라요. 저도 얼마 전에 처음 들었어요.”
108|
109|“누구한테?”
110|
111|“은인이요.”
112|
113|적천강은 청풍이 가리키는 방향을 따라 고개를 돌렸다.
114|
115|그리고 실눈을 뜨고 있는 젊은 놈과 눈이 딱 마주쳤다.
116|
117|“마, 이리와 봐.”
118|
119|
120|
121|* * *
122|
123|
124|
125|봤나? 순간 눈이 마주친 것 같긴 한데…….
126|
127|아냐, 못 봤어. 절대 못 봤어. 바로 눈 감았는데 그걸 어떻게 봐? 나는 눈을 감은 채 몸을 부들부들 떨었다.
128|
129|마치 내상을 다스리기 위해 안간힘을 쓰는 것처럼.
130|
131|혹시 몰라 신음도 추가했다.
132|
133|“끄으읍!”
134|
135|“마, 이리 와 보라고.”
136|
137|침착하자.
138|
139|그냥 넘겨짚는 말이다. 여기서 냉큼 넘어가면 삼류다.
140|
141|이럴 때일수록 항문에 힘을 빡 주고 열연을 이어 가야 절정 고수다.
142|
143|“흐으으읍!”
144|
145|“억지로 힘주지 마라. 그러다가 똥 나오는 놈 여럿 봤다.”
146|
147|그것도 그러네. 적천강의 꿀팁에 나는 살짝 힘을 풀었다.
148|
149|“허으으읍!”
150|
151|“허어, 그놈 참. 마지막이다. 네가 올래, 노부가 갈까?”
152|
153|마지막. 겨우 이런 단어에 속으면 안 된다.
154|
155|마지막의 마지막까지 버텨야 한다.
156|
157|“노부가 가지 뭐. 넌 오늘 죽었다.”
158|
159|“……제가 가겠습니다.”
160|
161|나는 눈물을 머금고 눈을 떴다. 불길이 활활 쏟아지는 두 눈이 나를 노려보는 중이었다.
162|
163|실로 화왕(火王)이라는 별호에 어울리는 모습이다.
164|
165|‘시바, 화왕이라니.’
166|
167|형이 여기서 왜 나와…….
168|
169|열 번, 스무 번을 생각해도 도무지 믿기지 않는 상황.
170|
171|그러나 현실은 변하지 않는다. 저 땅딸막한 노인이 바로 천하에서 스무 손가락 안에 들어가는 초절정 고수, 화왕이다.
172|
173|‘어쩐지 처음부터 촉이 오더라.’
174|
175|모르긴 몰라도 이 자리에 있는 사람들 중 그의 정체를 가장 처음 알아차린 사람이 나일 것이다.
176|
177|적천강의 내력이 밀려 들어온 순간, 시스템이 의미심장한 말을 던졌으니까.
178|
179|띠링.
180|
181|
182|
183|- 당신의 [열양지기]가 열렬히 호응합니다.
184|
185|- 신체 내부에 침투한 공력과 동화됩니다.
186|
187|- 공력이 미약하게 상승합니다.
188|
189|
190|
191|눈 깜짝할 사이에 벌어진 일. 처음에는 산 채로 통구이가 되나 싶었는데, 금방 국밥 한 그릇 먹은 것처럼 뱃속이 뜨뜻해지더니 공력까지 상승했단다.
192|
193|‘뭐여, 이게.’
194|
195|처음에는 얼떨떨하면서도 좋은 게 좋은 거지, 생각했는데 곰곰이 생각해 보니 그렇게 태평할 때가 아니었다.
196|
197|‘잠깐만. 내 열양지기는 열화신단을 먹고 생긴 건데.’
198|
199|같은 열양지기라고 해서 타격을 안 받는다는 게 말이 되나. 심지어 흡수까지 해 버렸다.
200|
201|잠깐 치열한 고민이 있었지만 얼마 지나지 않아 결국 한 뿌리에서 나온 동류(同流)이기 때문이라는 결론이 나왔다.
202|
203|그건 저 노인네가 열화문 소속이라는 말인데, 내가 알기로 열화문은 일인전승이며 당대 문주가 아마…….
204|
205|‘화왕…… 에이, 그건 말도 안 되지. 사십 년 가까이 잠수 타고 있던 양반이 여길 왜 와?’
206|
207|그때만 해도 그렇게 생각했다.
208|
209|암 환자가 거치는 5단계의 심리 중 첫 단계는 ‘부정’이라더라. 나도 마찬가지다.
210|
211|다만 차이점이 있다면 5분도 채 되지 않아 마지막 단계인 ‘수용’에 접어들었다는 점이다.
212|
213|‘검성이랑 절친 사이에 정마대전 당시 구화산에 살았고 마교도들이 불을 질러서 싹 다 죽여 버렸고…….’
214|
215|시벌, 화왕이네?
216|
217|적천강과 청풍의 대화를 들을수록 정체가 확실해졌다.
218|
219|당사자의 입으로 자신이 직접 화왕이라고 밝히진 않았지만, 이건 모르는 게 병신인 수준이다.
220|
221|그렇게 마침내 수용 단계에 다다르자 등골이 서늘해졌다.
222|
223|‘좆 됐다.’
224|
225|내 일섬으로 몸의 절반이 날아간 채 죽은 조필의 모습이 떠오른다. 인벤토리에 넣어 둔 [이름 없는 검]과 [화염신장]의 비급도 마찬가지.
226|
227|심지어 열화신단은 이미 꿀꺽해서 단전에 잘 보관하고 있다.
228|
229|‘아, 속 쓰려.’
230|
231|조필이 저 노인네의 제자여도 문제고, 아니어도 문제다.
232|
233|머릿속이 복잡해 도살장에 끌려가는 소처럼 천천히 발걸음을 떼는 내게 적천강이 손가락을 폈다.
234|
235|“셋을 센다. 하나.”
236|
237|쐐애애액!
238|
239|혼신의 힘을 다해 쇄도했다. 화왕이 별 미친놈 다 보겠다는 표정으로 입을 열었다.
240|
241|“마.”
242|
243|“넵!”
244|
245|“깜짝이야, 귀 안 먹었으니까 작게 말해!”
246|
247|빡! 경쾌한 타격음과 함께 뒤통수가 얼얼해진다. 무림에서 이런 식으로 얻어맞아 보는 건 처음이다.
248|
249|물론 항의할 생각 따위는 없다. 상대는 성질 더러운 초절정 고수니까.
250|
251|입을 꾹 다무는 나를 바라보는 적천강의 눈이 가늘어진다.
252|
253|“이놈 보게. 아까보다 훨씬 얌전해졌는데?”
254|
255|“아닙니다.”
256|
257|“아니기는. 노부를 속이느니 차라리 귀신을 속여라. 눈깔 뜨는 것부터가 다른데.”
258|
259|곁에 있던 청풍이 걱정스러운 표정으로 다가왔다.
260|
261|“은인, 몸은 괜찮으세요?”
262|
263|몸은 괜찮은데. 마음이 죽어 간다.
264|
265|나는 반쯤 죽어 가는 목소리로 대답했다.
266|
267|“네. 그럭저럭…….”
268|
269|“그럭저럭이라고?”
270|
271|깜빡이도 안 켜고 고개를 쑥 내민 적천강이 나를 위아래로 훑었다.
272|
273|“흠. 그러고 보니 한 식경은 꼼짝 못 하고 운기를 해야 할 놈이 왜 이렇게 멀쩡해?”
274|
275|왜 멀쩡하긴. 열화신단을 흡수했으니까 그렇지.
276|
277|하지만 그렇게 대답할 수는 없었다. 수상쩍다는 듯 바라보는 시선에 입 안이 바짝바짝 탄다.
278|
279|“아까부터 볼수록 묘한 놈일세. 네놈이 어디 문하라고?”
280|
281|“태원진갑니다.”
282|
283|“태원진가…… 분명 어디서 들어 봤는데.”
284|
285|미간을 좁히고 있던 적천강이 아, 하고 탄성을 토했다.
286|
287|“화양검(火魎檢)이었던가? 맞아, 진백양인가 하는 그 녀석이 태원진가 출신이었지.”
288|
289|화양검 진백양. 바로 대장로다.
290|
291|저 이름이 여기서 튀어나올 줄이야.
292|
293|대답을 요구하는 눈빛에 나는 입술을 핥았다.
294|
295|“맞습니다.”
296|
297|“오다가다 몇 번 마주쳤는데 괜찮은 녀석이었어. 어딘가 음울한 구석이 있기는 했지만, 뭐 그때야 다들 그랬으니까. 예의도 깍듯했고.”
298|
299|사람에게 남는 건 추억밖에 없다. 특히 적천강처럼 살아갈 날이 얼마 남지 않은 늙은이라면 더더욱.
300|
301|‘그런데 왜 하필 그 추억이 대장로냐.’
302|
303|심지어 썩 괜찮은 기억으로 남아 있는 모양이다.
304|
305|하긴, 얼마 전까지만 하더라도 대장로가 그런 일을 벌이리라고는 아무도 예상하지 못했다.
306|
307|심지어 정마대전 당시의 그는 유력한 가주 후보에 꼽힐 정도로 고강한 무공에다가 인망도 두터웠으니까.
308|
309|“네 녀석도 성취를 보아하니 태원진가의 핏줄 같은데. 화양검과는 무슨 관계더냐?”
310|
311|“제 작은 조부님 되시는데요.”
312|
313|실상은 죽고 죽이는 관계였지만, 결코 거짓말을 한 건 아니다.
314|
315|한 핏줄이라는 말에 적천강의 눈빛이 한결 누그러졌다.
316|
317|“오호. 그래?”
318|
319|“옙.”
320|
321|“나이는 몇인고?”
322|

Stay calm.

Whoosh!

“Yes!”

Smack!

Blade of Flowers Jin Baekyang.

[P157]

[P158]
“Oh-ho. Is that so?”

[P159]
“Yes, sir.”

[P160]
“How old are you?”

[P161]
“Twenty this year. I’ve just come of age.”

[P162]
“You seem to have learned Scorching Yang Qi. Did the Blade of Flowers teach you?”

[P163]
“…Yes.”

[P164]
He had given me some instruction about two months ago at Eight Spring Gorge.

[P166]
“Your attainment is remarkable for your age. You’ve far surpassed the Blade of Flowers in his youth.”

[P167]
Jeok Cheongang was even offering me compliments now.

[P168]
The atmosphere had become warm and friendly overall.

[P169]
Then he opened his mouth again.

[P170]
“So, is he doing well?”

[P171]
“Uh…”

[P172]
*Well, he’s doing fine in his grave, I suppose.*

[P173]
“His martial arts must have improved considerably by now. Should I stop by and see him while I’m here?”

[P174]
“About that…”

[P175]
*You can visit, but you won’t be seeing his face.*

The Head Elder’s grave was in one corner of the Jin Family of Taiyuan’s cemetery—in other words, the family cemetery.

[P177]

[P178]
“I suppose I should have a drink with him. It’s been a long time since we last met. Surely he won’t treat me coldly.”

[P179]
I imagined Jeok Cheongang pouring liquor beside the Head Elder’s grave.

[P180]
*Damn it. I can’t keep this up.*

[P181]
I took a deep breath.

[P182]
“Um, there’s something I need to tell you.”

[P183]
“What is it? Go ahead.”

[P184]
“He passed away.”

“…What?”

[P186]
“Just a couple of months ago, unfortunately.”

Jeok Cheongang was silent for a moment before muttering, “Already? He was still going strong.”

[P188]
“…”

[P189]
*Going strong? He was over eighty.*

[P190]
Of course, he had possessed powerful internal energy. If he had stayed out of trouble, he might have lived another twenty years.

[P191]
“What happened?”

[P192]
“He fell in battle.”

[P193]
“He fell in battle?”

[P194]
A trace of anger appeared in Jeok Cheongang’s eyes.

[P195]
“Was it the Demonic Cult bastards?”

[P196]
“No. The circumstances were complicated and sensitive, so it’s difficult to explain.”

[P197]
“Do you know who killed him?”

[P198]
“…”

[P199]
“Did you avenge him? From the Jin Family of Taiyuan’s perspective, he was the kind of bastard they could grind up and eat, bones and all, and still not be satisfied.”

[P200]
Listening to him made me feel as if my bones were turning to jelly.

[P201]
I lowered my head silently with a sorrowful expression. Sensing the subdued atmosphere, Jeok Cheongang stopped speaking.

[P202]
*Good. Perfect. Hyuk Mujin being unconscious was a stroke of genius.*

[P203]
If he had been awake, he would have been shooting me sidelong glances and practically shouting, *This is the culprit. He killed him.*

[P204]
*All right. As soon as I get out of here, I’m getting the hell away. Maybe I should just use Logout altogether.*

[P205]
Then, in the next moment, I realized something.

[P206]
“Huh? Blade of Flowers Jin Baekyang—isn’t he the person you killed, Benefactor? Right?”

[P207]
I had forgotten about that bastard.

## Adjudicator rules

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

For `REPAIR`, write the smallest complete replacement needed for that hunk. It must be natural English and fully source-faithful.

## Glossary

Korean **keys** are binding unless the source uses that string in a different ordinary-language sense. Glossary **English** is not a license for a calque (`presiding chair`). If SOL is a natural recast of the same sense, keep SOL.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

A crisp blow left the back of my head throbbing. It was the first time I had ever been hit like that in the Murim.

[P123]
Of course, I had no intention of protesting. My opponent was an irritable Supreme Peak master.

[P124]
Jeok Cheongang narrowed his eyes as I kept my mouth shut.

[P125]
“Well, look at you. You’re much quieter than before.”

[P126]
“No, I’m not.”

[P127]
“Don’t lie to this old man. You’d have better luck deceiving a ghost. Even the way you opened your eyes was different.”

[P128]
Cheongpung approached with a worried expression.

[P129]
“Benefactor, are you all right?”

[P130]
*My body is fine. My soul is dying.*

[P131]
I answered in a half-dead voice.

[P132]
“Yes. More or less…”

[P133]
“More or less?”

[P134]
Without so much as a turn signal, Jeok Cheongang stuck his head in and looked me up and down.

[P135]
“Hmm. Now that I think about it, why are you so fine? You should have been unable to move and forced to circulate your energy for at least half an hour.”

[P136]
*Why am I fine? Because I absorbed the Blazing Flame Divine Pill.*

[P137]
But I could not say that. Under his suspicious gaze, my mouth went dry.

[P138]
“You’re a strange one, the more I look at you. Which sect are you from?”

[P139]
“I’m from the Jin Family of Taiyuan.”

[P140]
“The Jin Family of Taiyuan… I’m sure I’ve heard of it somewhere.”

[P141]
Jeok Cheongang furrowed his brow for a moment, then exclaimed, “Ah!”

[P142]
“Was it the Blade of Flowers? That’s right. That fellow Jin Baekyang was from the Jin Family of Taiyuan.”

[P143]
Blade of Flowers Jin Baekyang.

[P144]
He was the Head Elder.

[P145]
I never expected that name to come up here.

[P146]
Under Jeok Cheongang’s demanding gaze, I licked my lips.

[P147]
“That’s right.”

[P148]
“I ran into him a few times in my travels. He was a decent fellow. He had a somewhat gloomy side, but everyone was like that back then. He was also unfailingly courteous.”

[P149]
All that remained to a person were their memories, especially for an old man like Jeok Cheongang, who did not have many years left to live.

[P150]
*But why did that memory have to be of the Head Elder?*

[P151]
Apparently, he remembered him quite fondly.

[P152]
Then again, until recently, no one would have expected the Head Elder to do what he had done.

[P153]
During the Great Faction War, his martial arts had been formidable enough to make him a leading candidate for Family Head, and he had been widely respected.

[P154]
“Judging by your attainment, you carry the Jin Family of Taiyuan’s blood. What is your relationship with the Blade of Flowers?”

[P155]
“He’s my great-uncle.”

[P156]
In reality, we had been locked in a relationship of killing or being killed. But I was not technically lying.

[P157]
At the mention of shared blood, Jeok Cheongang’s eyes softened.

[P158]
“Oh-ho. Is that so?”

[P159]
“Yes, sir.”

[P160]
“How old are you?”

[P161]
“Twenty this year. I’ve just come of age.”

[P162]
“You seem to have learned Scorching Yang Qi. Did the Blade of Flowers teach you?”

[P163]
“…Yes.”

[P164]
He had given me some instruction about two months ago at Eight Spring Gorge.

[P165]
He had been so enthusiastic about it that Sword Energy had nearly split my head open.

[P166]
“Your attainment is remarkable for your age. You’ve far surpassed the Blade of Flowers in his youth.”

[P167]
Jeok Cheongang was even offering me compliments now.

[P168]
The atmosphere had become warm and friendly overall.

[P169]
Then he opened his mouth again.

[P170]
“So, is he doing well?”

[P171]
“Uh…”

[P172]
*Well, he’s doing fine in his grave, I suppose.*

[P173]
“His martial arts must have improved considerably by now. Should I stop by and see him while I’m here?”

[P174]
“About that…”

[P175]
*You can visit, but you won’t be seeing his face.*

[P176]
The Head Elder’s grave was in one corner of the Jin Family of Taiyuan’s cemetery—in other words, the family cemetery.

[P177]
The family’s senior members had vehemently opposed it, but Jin Wikyung had pushed it through. He had felt guilty about the mistake made by his grandfather, the former Family Head.

[P178]
“I suppose I should have a drink with him. It’s been a long time since we last met. Surely he won’t treat me coldly.”

[P179]
I imagined Jeok Cheongang pouring liquor beside the Head Elder’s grave.

[P180]
*Damn it. I can’t keep this up.*

[P181]
I took a deep breath.

[P182]
“Um, there’s something I need to tell you.”

[P183]
“What is it? Go ahead.”

[P184]
“He passed away.”

[P185]
“…What?”

[P186]
“Just a couple of months ago, unfortunately.”

[P187]
Jeok Cheongang was silent for a moment before muttering, “Already? He was still going strong.”

[P188]
“…”

[P189]
*Going strong? He was over eighty.*

[P190]
Of course, he had possessed powerful internal energy. If he had stayed out of trouble, he might have lived another twenty years.

[P191]
“What happened?”

[P192]
“He fell in battle.”

[P193]
“He fell in battle?”

[P194]
A trace of anger appeared in Jeok Cheongang’s eyes.

[P195]
“Was it the Demonic Cult bastards?”

[P196]
“No. The circumstances were complicated and sensitive, so it’s difficult to explain.”

[P197]
“Do you know who killed him?”

[P198]
“…”

[P199]
“Did you avenge him? From the Jin Family of Taiyuan’s perspective, he was the kind of bastard they could grind up and eat, bones and all, and still not be satisfied.”

[P200]
Listening to him made me feel as if my bones were turning to jelly.

[P201]
I lowered my head silently with a sorrowful expression. Sensing the subdued atmosphere, Jeok Cheongang stopped speaking.

[P202]
*Good. Perfect. Hyuk Mujin being unconscious was a stroke of genius.*

[P203]
If he had been awake, he would have been shooting me sidelong glances and practically shouting, *This is the culprit. He killed him.*

[P204]
*All right. As soon as I get out of here, I’m getting the hell away. Maybe I should just use Logout altogether.*

[P205]
Then, in the next moment, I realized something.

[P206]
“Huh? Blade of Flowers Jin Baekyang—isn’t he the person you killed, Benefactor? Right?”

[P207]
I had forgotten about that bastard.

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). **Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.

# Adjudication Task — Chapter 173

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃173화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|“그럼……?”
  6|
  7|청풍의 놀라움이 섞인 눈빛에 화왕(火王) 적천강은 희미하게 웃어 보였다.
  8|
  9|“나에 대해 들은 바가 있느냐?”
 10|
 11|“할아버지께서 가끔 말씀해 주셨어요.”
 12|
 13|“오호. 그 친구도 나를 잊지 않았나 보구나. 뭐라 하더냐?”
 14|
 15|“무공은 강한데 성격이 좀, 많이 더럽다고 하셨는데요.”
 16|
 17|“…….”
 18|
 19|사실 적천강은 사교성이 그리 좋은 편은 아니었다. 아니, 좋지 않은 정도가 아니라 사실 끔찍한 수준이다.
 20|
 21|어린 시절 온갖 험한 꼴을 겪은 터라 사람에 대한 불신이 뿌리에 박혀 있었고, 그 후에는 괴팍한 성격의 사부 밑에서 자랐다. 그러니 어쩌면 당연한 일일지도 몰랐다.
 22|
 23|“정마대전 때도 하루가 멀다 하고 시비가 붙으셨다고 하던데. 당시 구파일방의 후기지수들은 한 대씩 다 때려 보셨을 거라고…….”
 24|
 25|“크흠, 다 때리긴 누가! 그리고 그때는 젊었으니 그런 것이다. 원래 혈기왕성할 때는…….”
 26|
 27|“당시 환갑이셨던 걸로 아는데요.”
 28|
 29|“커흐흐흠!”
 30|
 31|본전도 못 건진 적천강이 헛기침만 하고 있을 때, 청풍이 한마디를 덧붙였다.
 32|
 33|“그래도 알고 보면 선한 분이니 혹 뵙게 되거든 당신을 대하듯이 하라고 하셨어요.”
 34|
 35|적천강의 입꼬리가 실룩거렸다.
 36|
 37|“음, 매종학 그 친구가 역시 나를 잘 알아.”
 38|
 39|적천강이 정마대전에서 활약한 기간은 일 년 남짓.
 40|
 41|초절정 고수인 두 사람이 같은 전장에 참여하는 일은 드물었고, 매종학과는 열 번 정도 만났을 뿐이지만 지기(知己)라 부를 수 있는 관계인 것은 확실했다.
 42|
 43|‘손자 교육도 아주 잘 시켜 놨군.’
 44|
 45|한데 잠깐, 그가 혼인을 했던가?
 46|
 47|적천강은 청풍의 얼굴을 가만히 뜯어봤다.
 48|
 49|기억 속에 남아 있는 매종학의 얼굴과는 닮은 구석이 하나도 없다.
 50|
 51|‘친손자는 아닌 것 같은데…….’
 52|
 53|뭐, 상관없는 일이다.
 54|
 55|핏줄이 섞였건 안 섞였건 녀석이 그의 후인인 것은 확실해 보였으니까.
 56|
 57|특히 하는 행동이나 말본새를 보면 피가 아니라 영혼이 섞였다고 해도 과언이 아니다.
 58|
 59|적천강은 흐뭇한 웃음을 지으며 청풍에게 말했다.
 60|
 61|“내 오늘 아주 든든한 손주 하나가 생겼구나. 자, 그럼 이 할아비에게 큰절 한 번 올려 보거라.”
 62|
 63|“네?”
 64|
 65|고개를 갸우뚱거린 청풍이 되물었다.
 66|
 67|“왜요?”
 68|
 69|“……왜요라니?”
 70|
 71|순간 당황한 적천강이 말을 더듬었다.
 72|
 73|“매종학이 그 친구가 자신을 대하듯 나를 대하라고 하지 않았더냐?”
 74|
 75|“네.”
 76|
 77|“인석아, 그럼 손주가 할아비를 봤으면 큰절을 올려야지.”
 78|
 79|“저희 할아버지는 그런 거 신경 안 쓰세요. 앞뒤 꽉 막힌 노인네들이나 허례허식에 집착한다고 하셨어요.”
 80|
 81|“……!”
 82|
 83|졸지에 앞뒤 꽉 막힌 노인네가 된 적천강이 몸을 부르르 떨었다.
 84|
 85|“이런 걸 뭐라고 하더라. 얼마 전에 배웠는데.”
 86|
 87|골똘히 생각에 잠겨있던 청풍이 이마를 탁 쳤다.
 88|
 89|“아, 맞다. 꼰대!”
 90|
 91|“꼰, 뭐?”
 92|
 93|“꼰대요. 비슷한 말로 꼰머가 있대요.”
 94|
 95|뭐? 꼰대? 꼰머? 듣기에도 별로고, 어감도 별로다.
 96|
 97|정확히 무슨 말인지는 모르겠으나 맥락은 알 것 같았다.
 98|
 99|‘내가 너무 산에만 틀어박혀 있었나.’
100|
101|장강의 뒷물결은 상상 이상으로 강했다. 그렇다고 하나뿐인 지기의 손주 놈을 두들겨 팰 수도 없고…….
102|
103|적천강은 머리가 띵해지는 걸 느끼며 입을 열었다.
104|
105|“그게 요즘 젊은 놈들 사이에서 유행하는, 뭐 그런 거냐?”
106|
107|“몰라요. 저도 얼마 전에 처음 들었어요.”
108|
109|“누구한테?”
110|
111|“은인이요.”
112|
113|적천강은 청풍이 가리키는 방향을 따라 고개를 돌렸다.
114|
115|그리고 실눈을 뜨고 있는 젊은 놈과 눈이 딱 마주쳤다.
116|
117|“마, 이리와 봐.”
118|
119|
120|
121|* * *
122|
123|
124|
125|봤나? 순간 눈이 마주친 것 같긴 한데…….
126|
127|아냐, 못 봤어. 절대 못 봤어. 바로 눈 감았는데 그걸 어떻게 봐? 나는 눈을 감은 채 몸을 부들부들 떨었다.
128|
129|마치 내상을 다스리기 위해 안간힘을 쓰는 것처럼.
130|
131|혹시 몰라 신음도 추가했다.
132|
133|“끄으읍!”
134|
135|“마, 이리 와 보라고.”
136|
137|침착하자.
138|
139|그냥 넘겨짚는 말이다. 여기서 냉큼 넘어가면 삼류다.
140|
141|이럴 때일수록 항문에 힘을 빡 주고 열연을 이어 가야 절정 고수다.
142|
143|“흐으으읍!”
144|
145|“억지로 힘주지 마라. 그러다가 똥 나오는 놈 여럿 봤다.”
146|
147|그것도 그러네. 적천강의 꿀팁에 나는 살짝 힘을 풀었다.
148|
149|“허으으읍!”
150|
151|“허어, 그놈 참. 마지막이다. 네가 올래, 노부가 갈까?”
152|
153|마지막. 겨우 이런 단어에 속으면 안 된다.
154|
155|마지막의 마지막까지 버텨야 한다.
156|
157|“노부가 가지 뭐. 넌 오늘 죽었다.”
158|
159|“……제가 가겠습니다.”
160|
161|나는 눈물을 머금고 눈을 떴다. 불길이 활활 쏟아지는 두 눈이 나를 노려보는 중이었다.
162|
163|실로 화왕(火王)이라는 별호에 어울리는 모습이다.
164|
165|‘시바, 화왕이라니.’
166|
167|형이 여기서 왜 나와…….
168|
169|열 번, 스무 번을 생각해도 도무지 믿기지 않는 상황.
170|
171|그러나 현실은 변하지 않는다. 저 땅딸막한 노인이 바로 천하에서 스무 손가락 안에 들어가는 초절정 고수, 화왕이다.
172|
173|‘어쩐지 처음부터 촉이 오더라.’
174|
175|모르긴 몰라도 이 자리에 있는 사람들 중 그의 정체를 가장 처음 알아차린 사람이 나일 것이다.
176|
177|적천강의 내력이 밀려 들어온 순간, 시스템이 의미심장한 말을 던졌으니까.
178|
179|띠링.
180|
181|
182|
183|- 당신의 [열양지기]가 열렬히 호응합니다.
184|
185|- 신체 내부에 침투한 공력과 동화됩니다.
186|
187|- 공력이 미약하게 상승합니다.
188|
189|
190|
191|눈 깜짝할 사이에 벌어진 일. 처음에는 산 채로 통구이가 되나 싶었는데, 금방 국밥 한 그릇 먹은 것처럼 뱃속이 뜨뜻해지더니 공력까지 상승했단다.
192|
193|‘뭐여, 이게.’
194|
195|처음에는 얼떨떨하면서도 좋은 게 좋은 거지, 생각했는데 곰곰이 생각해 보니 그렇게 태평할 때가 아니었다.
196|
197|‘잠깐만. 내 열양지기는 열화신단을 먹고 생긴 건데.’
198|

## Adjudicator rules

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

For `REPAIR`, write the smallest complete replacement needed for that hunk. It must be natural English and fully source-faithful.

## Glossary

Korean **keys** are binding unless the source uses that string in a different ordinary-language sense. Glossary **English** is not a license for a calque (`presiding chair`). If SOL is a natural recast of the same sense, keep SOL.

Return exactly one JSON object and no Markdown fence or prose:

Reasons must name the veto, or say that SOL keeps sense and voice. Do not merely say one version is "better" or "more natural" without stating what changed.

Keep reasons brief. Do not adjudicate unchanged passages. Do not call tools.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.
